# NFS hardware fixtures

These files contain complete, unmodified UDP RPC payloads extracted from public
packet captures. No song audio is included. `nfs-provenance.json` records exact
source/destination addresses, capture timestamps, lengths, and SHA-256 hashes of
both each extracted payload and its source capture.

## Sources

- `nfs-s06-*`: [S06 load and play](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deep-Symmetry/dysentery/main/doc/assets/captures/S06-load-and-play/run.pcapng).
- `nfs-s13-*`: [S13 format ground truth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deep-Symmetry/dysentery/main/doc/assets/captures/S13-format-ground-truth/run.pcapng).
- `nfs-linkinfo-export-reply.bin`: [LinkInfo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deep-Symmetry/dysentery/main/doc/assets/LinkInfo.pcapng).

The [S06/S13 capture notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deep-Symmetry/dysentery/main/doc/assets/captures/README.md)
identify two CDJ-2000nexus players running firmware 1.44, captured 2026-07-29.
The corpus explicitly excludes software impersonators. The published S13 file
truncates streamed NFS audio frames, while mount and portmapper frames are
unchanged; both S13 payloads stored here are complete mount messages. LinkInfo
is the older hardware capture linked by the project's protocol investigation;
its exact firmware version is not established here.

## Facts established by the bytes

- S13 MOUNT xid 3 uses a six-byte XDR string `2f0043002f00`: `/C/` in UTF-16LE,
  with no terminator. Its two padding bytes are `0011`, not zero.
- S06 LOOKUP xid 4 names `Contents` using 16 UTF-16LE bytes, with no terminator.
  Xid 7 uses the same encoding for a track filename.
- Xid 4's LOOKUP response returns a 32-byte handle. Xid 5 preserves the first
  12 bytes and changes the remaining 20. Directory identity must survive this
  suffix change; it must not depend on the entire original opaque handle.
- S06 READ xid 12 requests exactly 8192 bytes at offset 3213, using AUTH_SYS.
- LinkInfo's EXPORT reply uses UTF-16LE paths and ASCII address/mask groups.

## Replay boundaries

Tests first parse original payloads directly. The serving test then replays
the original S06 LOOKUP with only its server-specific handle identity prefix
replaced by a locally issued identity. Its remaining handle suffix, auth data,
UTF-16LE filename, and XDR fields remain unchanged. It then replays the original
READ request after substituting the handle returned by that lookup. The test
file contains generated byte values, not captured media.

Conduction publishes software library roots `/` and `/conduction`; it does not
claim physical USB `/C/` or SD `/B/` slots. The captured `/C/` MOUNT tests verify
the incoming encoding and padding, not a Conduction USB emulation feature.
ASCII/UTF-8 requests remain an explicit compatibility extension. A mount's
encoding is recorded in its opaque handle and retained for subsequent names,
including Japanese UTF-16LE components that contain no zero byte.

These are offline compatibility checks against actual hardware messages.
The captures do not contain an authentic rekordbox software-server session and
do not replace an acceptance run serving Conduction's library to a real CDJ.
